title: Emergence of the Scrooge Ensemble in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model
abstract: The probabilistic nature of quantum measurement provides a direct window into the structure and complexity of many-body wave functions. When only part of a system is measured, the remaining degrees of freedom form an ensemble of post-measurement states whose statistical structure can reveal a stronger form of thermalization, known as deep thermalization. Recent numerical evidence suggests that this phenomenon is characterized by convergence of the projected ensemble to the Scrooge ensemble, a maximally random ensemble compatible with a given density matrix. In this Letter, we use the solvable Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model to unveil the mechanism by which the Scrooge ensemble emerges in many-body systems. By formulating measurement probabilities and post-measurement states in terms of path integrals, we analytically characterize all moments of the projected ensemble and show that they exactly match those of the Scrooge ensemble, even at short evolution times. We further connect this result to the saddle-point structure of the measurement path integral, which naturally generates the replica permutations underlying Scrooge statistics. Our results establish the solvable SYK model as a tractable setting for exploring universal statistics of quantum measurements in chaotic many-body dynamics.
summary: This theoretical paper uses the solvable Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model to study how measuring only part of a quantum system forces the remaining degrees of freedom into a statistically predictable state called the Scrooge ensemble. By mapping the problem onto path integrals and applying large-N techniques, the authors analytically prove that this emergence occurs even at very short times, establishing a key theoretical benchmark for understanding quantum measurement statistics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the statistical structure of post-measurement states when only a subsystem of a quantum system is measured, leading to the concept of deep thermalization.
main_result: The moments of the projected ensemble are shown to exactly match those of the Scrooge ensemble, confirming that the SYK model provides a tractable setting for studying this universal statistical behavior.
method: The analysis employs path integrals and large-N expansions applied to the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model to analytically characterize the moments of the projected states.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the solvable Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) Hamiltonian acting on Majorana fermions. The procedure involves initializing in a Thermofield Double state, evolving unitarily, and then performing projective measurements on one subsystem.
key_observables: Measurement probability ($p_m$), projected ensemble ($\{p_m, |\psi_mangle_A\}$), Shannon participation entropy ($S_1/N$), and the first moment of the reduced density matrix ($ho_A$).
important_parameters: Evolution time ($t$), system size ($N$), and coupling strength ($J$). The analysis explores limits like $N 	o \infty$ and short evolution times.
main_assumptions: The calculation relies on the large-N limit, self-averaging properties of the SYK partition function, and assumptions regarding positive fermion parity for post-measurement states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic setup involving TFD state initialization and measurement (Fig. 1). Other figures show path-integral representations for probabilities and density matrices (Fig. 2), and numerical results tracking probability distributions and entropy as a function of time (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper develops the formalism by first setting up the path integral representation for measurement processes in the SYK model, deriving saddle-point equations for the partition functions ($Z_m$), and finally calculating observables like the participation entropy and the reduced density matrix ($ho_A$) to confirm agreement with the Scrooge ensemble statistics.
why_interesting: The connection between quantum measurements, deep thermalization, and universal random ensembles (Scrooge) is highly relevant for understanding information scrambling in strongly interacting quantum systems, which is a core topic in modern condensed matter theory.

Af- ter time evolution, projective measurements are performed on most pairs of Majorana fermions, yielding outcomes m and a post-measurement state |ψm⟩A. We analyze the distribution p(λ) of measurement outcomes with λN entries of +1, as well as the projected ensemble {pmpJ, |ψm⟩A}, where pJ is the distribution of random couplings.
